initial_prompts.name: 01_dwarf_proportions
initial_prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create original art direction exploration for the voxel dwarf colony game DEEPDRAFT. It should feel warm, handmade, playful and readable at isometric colony-game camera distance.
Medium: convincing true cubical voxel models rendered in orthographic 3D, not a painting of smooth low-poly models. All modeled surfaces have axis-aligned flat faces and deliberate square stepped edges. Suggest a consistent native 1:16 object voxel grid relative to larger world blocks. Use broad planar masses with only a few one-voxel notches. No rounded bevels, smooth cylinders, cones, spheres, noisy per-voxel checkerboarding or realistic texture maps.
Shared art direction: adult chibi dwarves, sturdy broad square heads with only tiny clipped voxel corners, short stocky torsos, big simple mitten hands and chunky boots, compact readable dark eyes under expressive brows, recognizable nose and beard. Convey adult artisans with character, not babies or anime faces. Hair and beards form 3–5 strong block clumps, not many concentric stair-step stripes. Clothes in muted teal and moss with warm rust/copper accents; honey oak end grain, dark chocolate bark, slate blue-gray stone, warm cream light. Limit each material to 3–4 clear color values. Large calm flat color areas. Restrained warm light with cooler fill, clear midtones, contact shadows. No bloom haze, deep crushed blacks, realistic grain, extra tiny greebles, franchise logos, or copied game UI. Original designs inspired by the user's wish for the friendly proportions of a voxel colony sim.
Professional art concept presentation, with generous spacing and very little readable typography. These are visual proposals rather than exact engineering diagrams.
Asset type: wide character art direction comparison sheet, landscape.
Background: light warm parchment, understated fine rules, clean studio shadows.
Title verbatim: "DEEPDRAFT — DWARF PROPORTIONS".
Show three equally sized columns, A, B, C. Each presents the SAME adult copper-bearded dwarf worker in teal tunic, simple brown belt, large dark boots, and a compact blocky pickaxe beside him. Keep each figure's total standing height identical so proportions can be compared honestly. Show a large front-three-quarter full-body view and a smaller side view for each.
A label "A · STOUT": adult worker with roughly three head heights total, broad shoulders, squat and capable.
B label "B · HEARTHFOLK": recommended chibi balance with roughly two and a half head heights total, broad almost rectangular head, notably shorter body, bold eyebrow and friendly curious eyes, expressive square mitten hands, oversized functional boots. Label below "RECOMMENDED".
C label "C · PLAYFUL": roughly two head heights total, largest squarish head and tiniest body, noticeably more toy-like but still an adult dwarf with beard.
The three silhouettes must visibly differ. Do not just change clothes or facial hair. A is longer-bodied, B stocky, C very head-heavy.
Along the bottom put three small adult variants of B: a female dwarf artisan with two chunky braids and a rust apron, an older dark-skinned dwarf with a broad gray beard, and a light-skinned dwarf with short dark hair and a moss tunic. Their faces are original and distinct; use similar chibi body proportions.
Small exact footer text: "BIG SHAPES · CLEAR FACES · QUIET DETAIL". No other text.

Background: light warm parchment and soft studio shadows.
Title verbatim: "DEEPDRAFT — HAND-HEWN TIMBER".
Hero assembly occupies the left half: a primitive log dining table and exactly FOUR separate low log stools at cardinal sides. The table stays centered on a subtle 3 by 3 world-block floor area; the whole table-and-four-stool arrangement is tucked close into a subtle 5 by 5 floor patch. Keep proportions compact and functional for adult chibi dwarves. Show one reference dwarf standing beside the assembly for scale, outside the floor patch.
The tabletop is still a single broad tree cross-section, but its outline is a blocky, irregular near-square octagon, a few large stepped corner cuts, one asymmetric bark lobe. It must read as timber rather than a box or perfectly round barrel. Top is relatively flat, with just 3 broken, off-center, angular growth-ring marks in low contrast; one clear dark drying split entering from an edge; one small knot. No concentric target/bullseye pattern. The under-support is a narrow central log pedestal. Stools follow the same broad, irregular block forms, dark coarse bark in 3 wide patches and simple exposed cut tops, with one off-center check, not concentric rings. This is starter whole-log construction, not advanced polished joinery or metal furniture.
Right upper: the EXACT same dining table silhouette and pedestal, with a small scratched game grid and six chunky contrasting playing pieces on top. Label "SAME TABLE · GAME TOP".
Right middle: a squat broad 3 by 3 primitive log workbench with one axe scar and one corner chip, distinctly below the tabletop in height; a stout voxel hand axe rests on it. Label "WORKBENCH".
Right lower: three short whole logs laid on their sides, using the same chunky bark and end-cut language; one stool shown from the back to expose the simple bark panels. Label "TIMBER + STOOL".
Keep all models intentionally simple enough to read when small. Main label "ONE SHAPE FAMILY". Footer "A FEW BIG IMPERFECTIONS". No barrels, fancy chairs, smooth circles, excessive rings, nails or tiny clutter.

Title in a small restrained margin: "DEEPDRAFT — A WARM PLACE BELOW".
Show a compact cutaway dwarven refuge built into chunky blue-gray layered rock at the edge of a woodland entrance. It should read like a possible colony game view, not a giant fantasy illustration. The terrain keeps LARGE cubic world blocks with broad quiet wall and floor planes. Objects and dwarves use a visibly finer consistent cubical grid. No interface, selection outlines or floating labels.
The focal point is a warmly illuminated 3 by 3 log dining/game table with exactly four nearby matching low log stools, a blocky irregular near-square-octagonal slab and a narrow central log pedestal, one drying split, almost no decorative grain. A plain log bed with muted teal blanket is partly visible along the back. A narrow simple settlement banner near the entry uses a plain geometric mountain motif, not a franchise emblem.

Composition has ample empty floor space for pathing, a clear foreground-to-background hierarchy and simple readable silhouettes. Strong charming game-model design with flat surfaces and generous forms. Avoid realistic stone bricks everywhere, micro-texture, volumetric fog, cinematic bloom, tiny scattered clutter or impossible furniture proportions. No glossy plastic or smoothly rounded figures. Small footer "CHUNKY FORMS · WARM PEOPLE · COOL STONE".

refinements.name: 02_hand_hewn_timber
refinements.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Edit this DEEPDRAFT timber concept sheet into a stricter, simpler voxel game art proposal. Preserve the title, layout, palette, character scale reference, hero dining table with exactly four stools, and the game-table variant. Keep the furniture compact.
The specific correction is to SIMPLIFY THE SHAPE AND SURFACE LANGUAGE. Current bark, grain, stone paving and clothing are far too noisy. Replace the many tiny shaded cubes and mottled color chips with big uninterrupted flat polygon faces, axis-aligned cubical construction, hard ninety-degree edges and flat vertex colors. No rounded bevels or simulated smooth surfaces. Give each material just three solid tones. No checkerboard texture or per-voxel ambient shadow grid across flat top faces. Model only silhouette steps, one drying crack, one knot, and a few broad bark strips. Cut wood tops should be quiet pale honey with just two incomplete angular grain arcs in muted brown. Remove all tiny grain scratches. Floor consists of exactly five by five LARGE simple plain slate tiles. The irregular tabletop still fills the middle three by three tiles; four low stools fit on the four immediately adjacent middle-side tiles. It is one broad log slab with four large stepped corner cuts and slight asymmetry; not a perfect circular disc.
Dining and game table share the exact same slab and narrow single central log pedestal; the game version differs only by a scratched board and six large counters. Clearly show the central narrow pedestal under both tables. The workbench is a SINGLE BROAD LOW SOLID LOG STUMP, no separate legs, no metal, no plank joinery. The side-laid timber has quiet flat dark bark with two broad ridges, simple angular ends. Keep the timber sheet attractive and warm, but its forms should look like an achievable deliberately low-detail voxel game render, not a highly detailed craft sculpture. Preserve the existing short labels verbatim.

refinements.name: 03_warm_refuge
refinements.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Edit the supplied DEEPDRAFT refuge concept, preserving its attractive isometric composition, five adult chibi dwarves, warm honey wood versus cool slate stone palette, teal clothing, lively social poses and welcoming underground mood.
The single art-direction correction is to make the scene MUCH SIMPLER and closer to real low-detail cubical voxel game assets. Remove the multiscale mosaic surface texture. Replace the thousands of tiny speckled cubes and chamfered faces with broad flat uninterrupted faces, hard 90-degree edges and quiet solid colors, only three flat tones per material. No painted realistic grain or microtile patterns. Keep all silhouettes and surfaces constructed of axis-aligned cubic voxel steps; do not switch to smooth low-poly cones, bevels or rounded geometry.
Terrain walls and floor use visibly LARGE world cubes, with only sparse silhouette steps and variation; the furniture and characters use the smaller 1:16 concept grid. Walls should not look like individual masonry bricks or a castle, but like mined voxel rock. Floor should read as large calm slate squares with no tiny paving. Tree crowns are 4–6 broad asymmetric stepped cubic leaf masses each, not hundreds of individually outlined cubes. Keep one oak, one pine, one berry bush and the small rabbit outside.
Simplify the dwarves' hair and beard into a handful of larger cubic clumps; retain clear eyes, warm faces, big hands and boots. Keep the same adult chibi proportions and distinct people.
The central table is one primitive thick hand-hewn log cross-section with a narrow central log pedestal, a blocky irregular outline, two faint broken grain arcs and one drying split. It has exactly FOUR small matching log stools, three seated dwarves and one free stool. Keep the woman bringing mugs nearby and the working dwarf at right. His workbench is one broad low solid log stump, not a fitted carpenter's bench on legs. The simple bed uses whole logs and one broad teal blanket.
Remove the wall display shelf, decorative bottles, storage chest, rugs, spare floor clutter and carved frame posts. Leave clear walking space. Keep the simple settlement banner and a small square stone campfire, plus only TWO primitive wooden wall torches. Avoid decorative objects unsupported by the existing game.
Keep the warm readable light but tone down bright orange saturation on the rock. Shadowed faces remain readable. The final image should demonstrate that charm comes from strong shapes, character gestures and carefully placed color, without needing dense detail or new decorative furniture. Preserve the exact DEEPDRAFT title and existing footer.
